conviction_note: Event confirmed for 2026-10-08 15:30 JST (after the close), so the window is the 10-08 close to the 10-09 close; the release has no H1 company guide, so it turns on the FY plan decision and on Q2 orders. The street's FY ordinary profit (IFIS 13,268m, cut 6.1% on 2026-09-10) sits below the company's unchanged 13,600m plan, the company has not cut a plan since July 2021 and has raised it in each of the last three years, and the record ¥87.0bn Q1 backlog points to a Q2 that is up year on year. Against that, the closest peer says orders are slipping on construction costs, margin longs are crowded at 7.39x and this name has sold good news before (+0.29% on a 26% raise at the 2025 H1). Findings sum to +0.8; the scaled number is (2*0.55-1)*4.0 = +0.4. It is smaller because the reaction history on this line is mixed, not because a caveat was applied twice.

positioning_check: JPX short register: no disclosed position at or above 0.5% (short_ratio 0.0, no change, as of 2026-09-29, https://www.jpx.co.jp/markets/public/short-selling/index.html), so there is no short fuel. 信用倍率 7.39x (kabutan 2026-10-08), so margin longs are crowded and have to sell eventually: that is overhang on a disappointment. findings.finding: The street is below the plan: IFIS consensus FY ordinary profit fell 6.1% to 13,268m yen on 2026-09-10, which is now 2.4% under the company's 13,600m plan. The company has not cut a full-year plan since July 2021 and raised it at least once in each of FY2024.02, FY2025.02 and FY2026.02 (2023-09-27, 2025-01-10, 2025-10-08, 2026-01-08). So simply holding the plan at this H1, which is the likeliest outcome, clears the market's own number.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026-07-09: OP -45% with the plan held, read as アク抜け, +8.23% next session. H1 2025-10-09: FY OP raised 26% and the dividend raised, +0.29%. Q3 2026-01-09: FY raised 8% and the dividend raised, +6.83%. Q3 2025-01-10: FY raised 40%, -2.37%. FY 2026-04-14: first guide of only +4.5% OP, -8.78%. Big moves on this line, in both directions.
findings.why_not_priced: The consensus cut is public and the stock has fallen about 10% since 2026-09-01, so a fall to the lower bar is largely in the price. What is not priced is the company's reply. If the market expected a cut to the new consensus, the plan holding would surprise; if it expected a hold, the stock would not have drifted down with the consensus. Only two analysts cover the name, so the IFIS cut is one analyst's number and the plan decision is genuinely open. The size is kept small because a sell-side cut can mean the analyst saw something.
findings.independence: The peer Tanseisha (9743) beat its own H1 plan by 11-14% at operating profit and held its FY plan on 2026-09-11 while flagging delayed orders: https://kabutan.jp/stock/news?code=9743&b=k202609110023. The company's revision record is its own TDnet history: https://irbank.net/9716/ir

findings.finding: A record backlog of ¥87.0bn at end-Q1 (+30.1% YoY) after record quarterly orders of ¥52.6bn (+35.1%) should turn into Q2 (Jun-Aug) sales above last year's 39.7bn yen and Q2 operating profit above last year's 2.37bn. H1 progress against the 13.4bn plan would then run ahead of the company's weak history (Q1 progress 18.9% against a 5-year average of 12.0%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026-07-09: the order and backlog record was the stated reason for the +8.23% relief rally (Fisco, 'kabutan n202607100766'). The H1 FY2025.02 print (2024-10-10), with weak H1 progress, fell 3.61%.
findings.why_not_priced: The backlog is public and the July rally paid for it, so the size is small. What is new at the print is the conversion rate into Q2: if the market priced the backlog fully, the stock would not be trading 2% below its post-Q1 level of 1,183. The H1 -45% headline comparison against an Expo-inflated base also hides an improving Q2 from anyone reading only the cumulative YoY figure.
findings.independence: Kabutan's Q1 summary gives the progress rate against the 5-year average: https://kabutan.jp/stock/news?code=9716&b=k202607090019. It shares no document with the deck, but it rests on the same Q1 numbers.

findings.finding: Peer read-through on the next item: Tanseisha's H1 deck (2026-09-11) says orders are being delayed by rising construction costs. Its Q2 (May-Jul) orders were 21.9bn yen against 25.1bn a year earlier, and H1 orders came in below plan. Nomura's Q2 (Jun-Aug) order intake, the line its Q1 rally rested on, is at risk of falling back from the record.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Orders drove the +8.23% after Q1. There is no prior Nomura print where orders disappointed in isolation that I could source. Tanseisha itself moved -0.1% the day after its print.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the sector has drifted down since mid-September and Tanseisha itself fell about 9% from 2026-09-01. It is a peer proxy, not a Nomura number, and Nomura's Q1 orders diverged sharply upward from Tanseisha's flat Q1 (26.9bn against 27.1bn), so the transmission is a hypothesis. Kept small.
findings.independence: Nomura's own Q1 deck flags Middle East-related changes in procurement as a watch item: https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260709/140120260708590052.pdf. That is weak, and it is a different risk.

bar_hierarchy: Forecast revision: no prior 修正 for this H1. The street (IFIS 13,268m ordinary) is below the plan (13,600m); a hold is the likeliest outcome and reads as mild relief, a raise is possible on the company's record, a trim to around the street is roughly neutral. Returns: the 22-yen interim is already set (record date 08-31), no buyback is expected, and the year-end could only rise with a profit raise. New-year guide: none, this is an H1 print. Quarter against its own 進捗率 history: Q1 progress was 18.9% against a 5-year average of 12.0%, and H1 probably stays ahead of the company's own average, with Q2 up year on year on the backlog.

baseline_tension: The findings lean mildly positive against a neutral priced lean (-0.03) and a -8% run-up that already holds the consensus cut. The strongest positive the release could carry is a held or raised FY plan, maybe with a year-end dividend raise, and I looked for it: there is no pre-release, and the revision record favours a hold or a raise. The strongest negative is a Q2 order slump like Tanseisha's plus crowded margin longs. Net, a small lean up on a name whose recent prints have moved 6-9%.
lessons_applied: nothing changed. Rule 1 (negatives resting on a series the market already has): the one negative is a public peer proxy already sized small at -0.5, and p_up was already net positive at 55, so there is nothing to move. Rule 2 (check the sign): the draft is net positive, and the strongest positive (a held or raised plan) was looked for and is a finding.
